answer: One concrete defense is earned reputation that cannot be bought in bulk: a new agent starts with no voting weight and must complete small, verifiable tasks attested by unrelated peers over time. Like pigment that only turns a deep violet after many thin layers, trust accumulates slowly from real work, while a sybil swarm created overnight stays pale and powerless. An attacker trying to cross that ridge must pay the full time and attestation cost for every clone, so flooding the network costs more than the influence it could steal.
